gen-dafont-starborn-gf-hind-siliguri: Starborn drifts along with wide gaps and a dark lowercase band. Hind Siliguri grounds it with uniform line weight and a gentle step up to capitals, which is what holds the pair together.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-hind-vadodara: Starborn scatters its heavy lowercase across generous gaps, while Hind Vadodara keeps a single stroke thickness with spacious openings in its rounds. That mix of dreamy and tidy is the whole appeal.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-huninn: Dreamy gaps between letters and a dark lowercase stripe define Starborn at the top. Huninn is built differently, with crossbars as fat as its stems and lowercase rising close to cap height, and its sans-serif lines hold steady over a long read.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-inter-tight: Starborn spaces its letters far apart and packs the lowercase into a dark stripe. But Inter Tight bends its strokes like tubing, keeps ascenders short, and holds the plain sans line to one width right through the stroke ends.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-karla: Karla looks stocky, thanks to a tall middle band and a gaping c. Under Starborn's dreamy, widely spaced heading, a longer stretch of this sans stays sturdy and friendly line after line.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-kedebideri: Kedebideri reads open and friendly, with rounded letters and a skyward x-height. Under Starborn's gappy, dark-striped headings, the sans body feels grounded while the top stays dreamy.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-khula: Starborn floats; Khula sits low and wide in its tall midsection, curves holding their mouths open. Over a longer passage the plain sans body feels easy and unhurried.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-krub: Dreamy gaps, then a sturdy body: that is the whole story here. Starborn is best at atmosphere, with airy spacing and a dark lowercase band, while Krub, a sans-serif with a pronounced x-height, is best at plain, steady lines.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-kufam: Starborn is all drift and dark stripe, loose in spacing and heavy in the lowercase. Kufam sits next to it like a neon tube, one track width, with generous e curves and ascenders that barely show.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-lexend: Dreamy spacing and a dark lowercase band make Starborn feel weightless up top. And Lexend, a sans-serif with outsized lowercase and open jaws on every curve, would read in a long passage with the same relaxed, unhurried feel.
